findings.reason: The protected source expresses the complete optimal result directly as sum(nums) - min(nums) * len(nums). It uses the standard relative-decrement equivalence, performs only the necessary aggregates, has clear conventional naming, and cannot be materially improved without sacrificing clarity, so no inert candidate is justified.

Metadata consistently identifies public LeetCode problem 453 and its runnable nonempty Python-array contract. The O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary-space manifest claims match the minimum and sum scans, and Python integers safely cover the source's guaranteed 32-bit result.

The immutable native source is bound to verified submission 2064923881. It is algorithmically and textually identical to the protected app-local body: both compute the minimum once and return the same sum-minus-baseline product; only the annotation spelling and LeetCode class wrapper differ.

The 31-, 127-, and 511-value descending tiers span more than 16x and force a candidate-by-candidate minimum search to make quadratic comparisons. The current source passed all 7 opaque correctness executions and all three performance tiers at 1.00x the reference runtime. A correct quadratic minimum-search control passed every output but failed only the runtime verdict at 959.12x.

The Approach exactly derives the protected formula by subtracting the common increment, proving that each original value must contribute its independent distance above the original minimum, and summing those distances. Its O(n) time, O(1) space, alternatives, and numerical boundary notes all correspond to the reviewed target.

The hash-bound modular Reference was checked directly against the live public statement. It preserves the exact n - 1 increment operation, both source examples and the complete three-move explanation, all four constraints, and the 32-bit-result guarantee. The unsupported legacy third example was removed from the source sequence.
